audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings build the matchup around "his W armor passive" (spikes[1], early, whys[1], whys[2], whys[3], whys[5], wants.foe[0]) and the real passive, Granite Shield, is never mentioned once.
audit.why: Thunderclap is an active on 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s with an auto-attack reset — "Malphite attacks with such force that it creates a sonic boom. For the next few seconds, his attacks create aftershocks in front of him." Calling it an always-on passive removes the entire trading pattern: the entry concludes "extended auto-trading is already turning against you even at level 2", when in fact he has to spend a ten-second cooldown and everything outside that window is a free trade. Meanwhile the actual passive, Granite Shield, absorbs up to 10% of his max health and recharges if he is not hit for a few seconds — which is precisely the strip-then-commit sequencing the packet flags this matchup for missing.
audit.corrected: Thunderclap is a 10s active auto-reset, not a passive. Granite Shield is the passive: 10% of his max health, recharging when you stop hitting him. Poke it off with Tongue Lash and commit immediately — pausing lets it come back.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet-flagged: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and the one cooldown the full layer does track is Unstoppable Force at every stage including level 2.
audit.why: Three of Malphite's four cooldowns are flat at every rank and none of them are in the entry: Seismic Shard 8s, Ground Slam 7s, Thunderclap 10s down to 8s, Unstoppable Force 130/115/100s. The flat ones matter most because they never improve — the seven seconds after Ground Slam is the same window at level 3 and level 18. Gating level-2 trades on an ultimate he does not have is not advice.
audit.corrected: Seismic Shard flat 8s, Ground Slam flat 7s, Thunderclap 10s at rank 1, Unstoppable Force 130s at rank 1 against your Abyssal Dive's 21s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seismic Shard is described as "his Q slow" throughout; nothing says it steals Move Speed.
audit.why: Riot's text: "dealing damage upon impact and stealing Move Speed for 3 seconds." It is a two-way swing — he gets faster by exactly what you lose. That changes the decision after you eat one: the entry's advice to "bait a Q slow" then reposition assumes you can still walk away, when for three seconds he is faster than you were.
audit.corrected: Seismic Shard steals your Move Speed rather than only slowing you. After it lands, do not try to walk him down or walk away — wait the three seconds out.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ground Slam is never mentioned in the content layer, in either its cooldown or its effect.
audit.why: Ground Slam is a flat 7s that "reduces the Attack Speed of enemies for a short duration". Tahm Kench builds An Acquired Taste stacks off basic attacks, so an attack-speed cut is a direct tax on his ability to reach three stacks and arm Devour. It is the most relevant of Malphite's abilities to Tahm Kench's core mechanic and it is absent from the entry entirely.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam is flat 7s and cuts your attack speed, which slows An Acquired Taste stacking off autos. Step in during the seven seconds it is down.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json — Ground Slam; champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — An Acquired Taste

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet-flagged: Tahm Kench wins 53.03% but content win[] gives Malphite 4 stages to Tahm Kench's 1. The full layer's own phases give Malphite zero of seven.
audit.why: 1684 games at 53.03% is one of the larger samples in the table and it is a lane Tahm Kench wins. The two layers give completely opposite pictures of the same four stages — content says Malphite owns Levels 4-5, Level 6, First item and 2+ items; full says Tahm Kench owns First item and 2+ items and calls the rest Skill. Both cannot be right and the content version is the one contradicting the win rate.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 Skill, Level 6 Malphite (his ultimate genuinely arrives), First item and 2+ items Tahm Kench — matching both the win rate and the full layer.
sources: packet tahmkench.json — winRate 53.03, games 1684, defect "level chart contradicts data"; champ-data/tahmkench.full.js phases

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] calls Heartsteel an armour item and attributes it to Malphite: "Malphite's first armor item (Heartsteel or Iceborn Gauntlet)".
audit.why: Heartsteel is a health item and it is Tahm Kench's own prescribed first item in this very file's itemization block. Giving it to Malphite as armour is wrong twice over, and the conclusion drawn from it — that his first item "hard-caps your grey-health sustain" — has no mechanism behind it. Granite Shield scales with his max health, not with anything he buys against you, and it caps at 10% either way.
audit.corrected: Heartsteel is your item, not his. Nothing Malphite builds increases Granite Shield beyond 10% of his own maximum health.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json — Granite Shield; champ-data/tahmkench.full.js — itemization block prescribing Heartsteel for Tahm Kench

audit.whatIsWrong: "Abyssal Voyage" carries the roam plan in wants.you[2], `mid`, `late`, whys[4] and whys[6]; `late` also says Unstoppable Force "is instant".
audit.why: Tahm Kench has no Abyssal Voyage. And Unstoppable Force is a travelling dash of up to 1000 range — "Malphite launches himself to a location at high speed" — not an instant cast. The readable tell is the launch, which matters for a champion whose only reaction is a 21s Abyssal Dive.
audit.corrected: There is no global. Unstoppable Force travels up to 1000 range, so the launch is the tell.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — W Abyssal Dive, R Devour; champ-data/_kits/malphite.json — Unstoppable Force range 1000

audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags resistances-invalidated on Granite Shield ("raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here"). That looks like a derivation artifact from the percentHealth flag — Granite Shield is a shield sized as a percentage of his health, not a damage type that bypasses resistances. I did not write any itemization advice on that basis.

notes: The "W armor passive" error is the load-bearing one: it made the entry conclude that extended trading is lost from level 2 onward, which is how a 53.03% lane over 1684 games ended up with a chart giving Malphite four of seven stages. Thunderclap is a 10s active and Granite Shield — the actual passive, worth 10% of his max health and recharging out of combat — never appears in the entry at all. Three chart edits (content win[3], win[5], win[6]) are enum-style and will fail a strict +/-10% band; they need applying by hand. Note also that _missing-interactions.json's resistances-invalidated row for Granite Shield looks like a derivation artifact from its percentHealth flag rather than a real armour-bypass, so I deliberately wrote no itemization advice from it.
